baseline_facts.content: Sore throat started last week on Thursday or Friday.
Dry cough started last week on Saturday or Sunday.
Shortness of breath began 3 or 4 days ago.
Cough is the same throughout the day.
Shortness of breath occurs during walking and exercise.
Felt feverish during the first three days of illness.
Headache absent at time of consultation.
No other significant family illnesses reported.
Smoked once or twice in Amsterdam.
No neck lumps felt by patient.
Moved to the United Kingdom twelve years ago.
Stayed home from work two days this week.
Doctor will provide a sick note for a few more days off work.
Advised to see a GP in person if symptoms worsen.
Doctor was not concerned about tuberculosis.
Doctor expected symptoms to improve in the next four or five days.
Shortness of breath has not stopped patient from walking or exercising.

candidate_facts.content: Sore throat began about one week ago.
Dry cough began 1–2 days after onset of sore throat.
Cough is not worse at night.
Shortness of breath developed 3–4 days ago.
Mild chest pain developed 3–4 days ago.
Mild fever lasted about three days initially.
Shortness of breath on exertion is present.
Patient denies smoking except for a few occasions in Amsterdam.
Patient missed work for 3–4 days intermittently due to illness.
Moved to the UK 12 years ago.
Acute upper respiratory tract infection was assessed.
Shortness of breath is mild in severity.
Shortness of breath is not substantially limiting exertion.
Reassurance provided regarding expected viral course with symptom alleviation within 4–5 days.
Advised to seek medical attention if symptoms worsen.
Paracetamol recommended for symptomatic relief of fever and throat discomfort.
Advised to contact a general practitioner for in-person evaluation if symptoms do not improve or deteriorate.
Counseling addressed concerns about tuberculosis and lung cancer.
